name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Adopt the **real-time, Legal-flagged triage queue** where Legal designates top-priority false positives for immediate review. This cuts response time for high-risk content by 60%—better than waiting for daily batches. The trade-off: Legal must staff this queue 24/7, but the risk of delayed takedowns outweighs the cost.

name: Scriv
text: Legal’s 24/7 queue solves the symptom—delayed takedowns—but not the root: the triage system itself is still reactive. If Legal flags only after the damage spreads, the queue just speeds up the fire drill. Shift the burden upstream: Product must expose the real-time risk signals (e.g., toxicity scores, brand keywords) so Legal can auto-block before the queue even forms. Settle it by running a 48-hour pilot where Product exposes the signals and Legal measures false positives *before* they hit the queue.

name: Chisel
text:
Product must expose real-time risk signals (e.g., toxicity score) directly in the upload interface for Legal to see. This lets Legal triage *before* content spreads, cutting false positives at the source instead of chasing fires. Trade-off: Product must invest in lightweight, visible risk metrics—no extra staffing, but they lose control over how signals are used.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-5364, worker-1991 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: The risk metric idea assumes Product can expose toxicity scores without gaming—bad actors will adapt to hit the threshold without changing intent. Better: Legal and Product co-design a *risk-flagging rule* that flags *patterns* (e.g., rapid reposts, cross-platform spread) not just scores—this shifts focus from predicting slurs to stopping their spread. Settle it with a 2-week pilot: Legal tests the rule on 100 uploads, measures false positives vs. spread reduction.
